what_worked: Crowded-vs-profitable category framing and payback-period acquisition screening are genuinely original and decision-useful.
fix_next: Reconcile all median MRR values against the source data; most category and B2B/B2C medians are materially wrong.
verdict: Strong analytical arc undermined by widespread median-value errors across key slides.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: AI median $446 vs ref $503; SaaS $303 vs ref $200.50; Marketing $1,586 vs ref $2,369.50; Dev Tools $185 vs ref $635; Content Creation $1,254 vs ref $1,237.50 (close but others wrong); Health & Fitness $392 vs ref $662.50. Education cited as $2,142 vs ref $2,435. Slide 2: Average MRR $13,472 — total $15,596,344.59/1000 = $15,596.34, not $13,472. Slide 6: B2B/B2C median ratio claimed ~5.7x ($1,036/$181) but reference on-sale medians give 2.35x; the slide may use full dataset but the magnitude diverges substantially from reference multiples.

evidence.insight: Slide 3 crowded-vs-profitable mismatch, slide 4 momentum-vs-monetization cross-cut, slide 7 domain-rating proxy, and slide 8 payback-period screening each add a distinct analytical layer beyond simple description.
evidence.narrative: Clear arc from summary through category/momentum/geography/audience/authority to acquisition screening and five numbered recommendations. Each slide builds toward the acquisition-intelligence thesis. Recommendations on slide 9 tie back to specific earlier findings.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 sets scope and audience well. Slide 2 notes median-vs-mean skew and promises sample-size reporting. However, 241 missing country values and 274 missing category values are never quantified, which weakens geographic (slide 5) and category (slides 3-4) claims. No limitations slide.
evidence.accuracy: At least 6 of 8 category medians on slide 3 diverge materially from reference values. Average MRR on slide 2 ($13,472) does not match total revenue / 1000. B2B/B2C median gap on slide 6 is overstated relative to reference. Domain-rating r=0.54 is plausible but unverifiable against reference. The pattern of errors suggests a systematic computation issue.
evidence.visual: Consistent navy/orange palette throughout. Paired bar charts on slide 3 are effective. Card layouts on slides 6 and 8 are clean and scannable. Slide 2 has overlapping rendering artifacts (duplicated content). Charts generally well-labeled though n-counts on bars would strengthen them.
evidence.ai_slop: Minimal. Language is specific and data-tied. No decorative filler. Slide 2 duplication appears to be a rendering/export artifact rather than padding.

change_reason: Reduced bonus from 2 to 1: the acquisition-screening table is genuinely original but the pervasive median errors undercut the reliability that would justify a higher bonus. Reduced framing from 7 to 6.5: missing-data rates are never disclosed despite affecting ~25-29% of key columns. Other scores confirmed as appropriate.
